title: Antenatal Care for Uncomplicated Pregnancy
edition: NG201, published 19 August 2021; recommendations retrieved 12 October 2026
locator: Recommendations 1.1.4 to 1.1.10; schedule of appointments; recommendations on gestational diabetes and ultrasound scanning
scope: Pregnant women receiving routine antenatal care for an uncomplicated singleton pregnancy; this limited extraction covers booking, selected screening tests and routine ultrasound timing.
gaps: This international source must be reconciled with current Saudi maternity pathways, laboratory panels, haemoglobinopathy and infectious-disease screening programmes, vaccination policy, rhesus prophylaxis, diabetes guidance and referral thresholds. It does not support a complete medicine regimen in this extraction.

investigations.test: Booking blood tests and infectious-disease screening
investigations.question: Are anaemia, blood-group or rhesus risks, red-cell antibodies, HIV, syphilis or hepatitis B identified?
investigations.finding: Full blood count, blood group and rhesus D status, antibody testing and programme-based infectious-disease screening define baseline risks and follow-up needs.
investigations.rationale: NICE places these tests in the routine antenatal schedule so clinically important maternal and fetal risks are identified early.
investigations.timeframe: At the first booking appointment, targeted by 10+0 weeks

investigations.test: Routine fetal ultrasound
investigations.question: Are gestation, multiple pregnancy, aneuploidy-screening choices and fetal anatomy appropriately assessed?
investigations.finding: The 11+2 to 14+1 week scan dates the pregnancy and identifies multiple pregnancy; the 18+0 to 20+6 week scan screens fetal development and placental location.
investigations.rationale: NICE specifies these gestational windows for routine ultrasound in uncomplicated pregnancy.
investigations.timeframe: 11+2 to 14+1 weeks and 18+0 to 20+6 weeks

investigations.test: Gestational-diabetes risk assessment and oral glucose tolerance test when indicated
investigations.question: Does the woman meet risk criteria for gestational diabetes?
investigations.finding: Risk assessment at booking identifies who should be referred for oral glucose tolerance testing.
investigations.rationale: NICE directs risk assessment at booking and OGTT referral for women at risk.
investigations.timeframe: Risk assessment at booking; OGTT at 24+0 to 28+0 weeks when indicated

actions.instruction: Offer the first antenatal booking appointment by 10+0 weeks and plan the routine appointment schedule according to parity and individual need.
Do not routinely offer ultrasound scans after 28 weeks in an uncomplicated singleton pregnancy; use targeted imaging when growth, presentation or wellbeing concerns arise.

title: Asthma
sourceTitle: Asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and chronic asthma management (BTS, NICE, SIGN)
edition: NG245, published 27 November 2024; page updated November 2025
scope: Adults, young people and children with a history suggestive of asthma; this extraction covers immediate assessment, objective diagnostic testing and monitoring rather than acute-attack dosing.
gaps: Age-specific inhaler products, device doses, licensing, escalation steps, contraindications and acute-exacerbation regimens require the current linked algorithms, product information and Saudi formulary reconciliation. The page names ICS/formoterol but does not provide a complete product-specific dose, route, frequency, duration and contraindication set for this extraction.

investigations.test: Blood eosinophil count or fractional exhaled nitric oxide
investigations.question: Is there objective evidence supporting asthma in an adult with a suggestive history?
investigations.finding: An eosinophil count above the laboratory reference range or FeNO at least 50 ppb supports an adult diagnosis.
investigations.rationale: NICE recommends eosinophils or FeNO as the first objective step for adults.
investigations.timeframe: At diagnostic assessment, before inhaled corticosteroid treatment when feasible

investigations.test: Bronchodilator reversibility with spirometry
investigations.question: Is reversible airflow obstruction present when eosinophils or FeNO do not confirm asthma?
investigations.finding: An FEV1 increase of at least 12% and 200 mL, or at least 10% of predicted normal FEV1, supports diagnosis in adults.
investigations.rationale: NICE uses spirometric bronchodilator reversibility as the next adult diagnostic step.
investigations.timeframe: Promptly when initial objective testing is non-diagnostic

investigations.test: Peak expiratory flow variability or bronchial challenge
investigations.question: Can asthma be confirmed when spirometry is delayed or prior objective tests are non-diagnostic?
investigations.finding: PEF variability of at least 20% over twice-daily measurements for 2 weeks supports diagnosis; bronchial hyper-responsiveness supports diagnosis when asthma remains suspected.
investigations.rationale: NICE provides sequential alternatives when earlier testing is unavailable or inconclusive.
investigations.timeframe: PEF twice daily for 2 weeks; challenge testing after unresolved diagnostic uncertainty

actions.instruction: Treat immediately if the person is acutely unwell or highly symptomatic and perform available objective tests without delaying treatment.
Monitor symptoms, reliever use, oral corticosteroid courses and urgent-care attendance at every asthma review; check adherence and inhaler technique.

title: Atrial Fibrillation [Adapted from NICE]
edition: NG196, published 27 April 2021; last updated 30 June 2021
scope: Adults with suspected or confirmed atrial fibrillation; limited to confirmation, stroke and bleeding risk, cardiac assessment and high-level treatment selection.
gaps: Drug choice and dosing depend on renal function, age, weight, interacting medicines, valvular disease and product criteria. The source names anticoagulants and rate/rhythm medicines but this extraction does not provide a complete dose, route, frequency, duration and contraindication set. Saudi formulary and emergency cardioversion pathways require reconciliation.

investigations.test: 12-lead ECG and ambulatory ECG when needed
investigations.question: Is atrial fibrillation present and is paroxysmal AF being missed by a single tracing?
investigations.finding: A 12-lead ECG confirms AF after an irregular pulse; 24-hour or longer event monitoring may detect paroxysmal AF according to symptom frequency.
investigations.rationale: NICE defines ECG confirmation and symptom-frequency-based ambulatory monitoring.
investigations.timeframe: At suspicion; ambulatory monitoring promptly when the 12-lead ECG is non-diagnostic

investigations.test: CHA2DS2-VASc and ORBIT risk assessment
investigations.question: What are the person's stroke and absolute major-bleeding risks?
investigations.finding: The recorded scores support shared decisions on anticoagulation and modifiable bleeding risks.
investigations.rationale: NICE recommends CHA2DS2-VASc for stroke risk and ORBIT for bleeding risk.
investigations.timeframe: At diagnosis and when clinical circumstances change

investigations.test: Transthoracic or transoesophageal echocardiography when indicated
investigations.question: Is structural or functional disease present and would imaging change long-term management or cardioversion planning?
investigations.finding: Imaging may identify structural disease, refine management or support TOE-guided cardioversion.
investigations.rationale: NICE limits echocardiography to defined management-changing indications rather than routine stroke-risk stratification alone.
investigations.timeframe: Before management decisions that depend on cardiac structure or cardioversion strategy

actions.instruction: Use clinical risk profiles and patient preferences when discussing anticoagulation; offer a direct-acting oral anticoagulant at CHA2DS2-VASc 2 or above and consider one for men with score 1, subject to suitability and current product guidance.
Refer promptly for specialist management when treatment fails to control symptoms, within 4 weeks of failed treatment or recurrence after cardioversion.

title: Breast Cancer Management
sourceTitle: Early and locally advanced breast cancer: diagnosis and management
locator: Recommendations 1.2.1 to 1.3.5, treatment sections 1.8 to 1.14 and follow-up recommendations 1.15.1 to 1.15.4
scope: People with newly diagnosed early or locally advanced breast cancer; limited to pretreatment staging, tumour biomarkers, multidisciplinary treatment selection and surveillance.
gaps: Cancer treatment must be subtype-, stage-, comorbidity- and protocol-specific. The source names systemic therapies and schedules but this extraction does not reproduce full regimens, doses, routes, supportive care, interactions or contraindications. Current Saudi oncology protocols, licensing and multidisciplinary review are mandatory before approval.

investigations.test: Pretreatment axillary ultrasound with ultrasound-guided needle sampling when abnormal
investigations.question: Is regional nodal disease present before treatment planning?
investigations.finding: Abnormal nodes sampled under ultrasound may confirm nodal metastasis and alter surgical or systemic planning.
investigations.rationale: NICE recommends ultrasound evaluation of the axilla and guided sampling of abnormal nodes.
investigations.timeframe: Before definitive treatment planning

investigations.test: ER, PR and HER2 status at initial histopathological diagnosis
investigations.question: Which biologic subtype guides systemic treatment?
investigations.finding: Quantitative, quality-assured ER, PR and HER2 results classify the tumour and inform treatment selection.
investigations.rationale: NICE recommends simultaneous biomarker assessment so results are available to preoperative and postoperative MDTs.
investigations.timeframe: At initial histopathological diagnosis

investigations.test: Breast MRI only for defined preoperative indications
investigations.question: Is disease extent unclear on examination, mammography and ultrasound, or is breast-conserving surgery planning otherwise uncertain?
investigations.finding: MRI may better define extent in selected patients; routine MRI is not recommended.
investigations.rationale: NICE restricts preoperative MRI to management-changing uncertainty.
investigations.timeframe: Before surgery when specified indications are present

actions.instruction: Discuss systemic anticancer, surgical and radiotherapy options in a specialist multidisciplinary team using stage, receptor status, comorbidity, toxicity and patient preference.
actions.timeframe: Before treatment starts and when pathology changes the plan

actions.instruction: Offer annual mammography for 5 years after breast cancer or DCIS treatment and avoid routine ultrasound or MRI surveillance unless another indication exists.

title: Breast Cancer Screening Discussion
sourceTitle: USPSTF Breast Cancer: Screening Final Recommendation Statement
locator: Recommendation Summary and Practice Considerations: patient population, assessment of risk and screening tests
scope: Women and other persons assigned female at birth aged 40 years or older at average risk, including those with family history or dense breasts but excluding defined high-risk genetic, prior chest-radiation, prior breast-cancer and high-risk-lesion groups.
gaps: This United States recommendation is not a Saudi national screening pathway. It finds insufficient evidence for screening at age 75 or older and for supplemental ultrasound or MRI after a negative mammogram in dense breasts. Saudi eligibility, interval, modality, referral capacity and high-risk pathways require reconciliation.

investigations.test: Biennial screening mammography
investigations.question: Is an average-risk person aged 40 to 74 eligible for routine breast-cancer screening?
investigations.finding: The USPSTF recommends mammography every 2 years for women aged 40 to 74.
investigations.rationale: The Task Force judged this strategy to have moderate net benefit for this population.
investigations.timeframe: Every 2 years from age 40 through 74

investigations.test: Risk and scope assessment before applying the routine recommendation
investigations.question: Does the person have a genetic syndrome, prior high-dose chest radiation, previous breast cancer or a high-risk breast lesion requiring a different pathway?
investigations.finding: A high-risk feature places the person outside the scope of the routine USPSTF recommendation.
investigations.rationale: The recommendation explicitly excludes these high-risk groups.
investigations.timeframe: Before routine screening is selected

actions.instruction: Discuss expected benefit, false positives, overdiagnosis and the limits of evidence, then use the current local programme for ordering and follow-up.
Use clinical judgement for people aged 75 or older and for supplemental ultrasound or MRI in dense breasts because evidence is insufficient.

title: Cancer Pain Assessment and Support
sourceTitle: Palliative care for adults: strong opioids for pain relief
edition: CG140, published 23 May 2012; last updated 3 August 2016
scope: Adults with advanced and progressive disease who require strong opioids for pain, with the dosing extraction limited to opioid-naive patients without renal or hepatic comorbidity during initial titration.
gaps: This older NICE guideline does not provide a complete contraindication or interaction set and must be checked against current controlled-drug rules, product information, renal and hepatic guidance, bowel regimens, Saudi formulary and local palliative-care protocols. The extracted starting doses do not apply to opioid-tolerant patients or those with moderate to severe renal or hepatic impairment.

investigations.test: Structured pain, toxicity and organ-function assessment
investigations.question: What are the pain pattern, prior opioid exposure, renal and hepatic status, side effects and patient concerns?
investigations.finding: The assessment identifies whether the source's oral morphine titration example applies and what specialist input is needed.
investigations.rationale: NICE limits the example starting dose to patients without renal or hepatic comorbidity and requires frequent review of pain control and side effects.
investigations.timeframe: Before initiation and frequently during titration

investigations.test: Constipation and nausea review
investigations.question: Are predictable opioid adverse effects developing and is preventive or therapeutic support adequate?
investigations.finding: Constipation is expected in nearly all patients; nausea may occur during initiation or dose change.
investigations.rationale: NICE includes explicit management recommendations for opioid-related constipation and nausea.
investigations.timeframe: At initiation and every titration review

actions.instruction: For an opioid-naive adult without renal or hepatic comorbidity, NICE gives a typical oral morphine total daily starting dose of 20 mg to 30 mg, for example sustained-release morphine 10 mg to 15 mg twice daily, plus immediate-release morphine 5 mg orally as rescue during titration.
actions.timeframe: During initial titration with frequent review

actions.instruction: Adjust until pain control and side effects are balanced; seek specialist advice after unsuccessful adjustments and before prescribing strong opioids in moderate to severe renal or hepatic impairment.

medicines.indication: Background pain requiring a strong opioid during initial titration
medicines.group: Opioid-naive adults with advanced progressive disease and no renal or hepatic comorbidity
medicines.duration: Initial titration phase; adjust to response with frequent review
adjustments: Seek specialist advice before prescribing in moderate to severe renal or hepatic impairment
Individualise after assessing prior opioid exposure and adverse effects
monitoring: Sedation and signs of opioid toxicity

medicines.indication: Rescue treatment for breakthrough pain during initial titration
medicines.group: Opioid-naive adults with advanced progressive disease and no renal or hepatic comorbidity
medicines.frequency: As rescue doses for breakthrough pain during titration; exact maximum frequency requires local prescribing protocol
adjustments: Seek specialist advice before prescribing in moderate to severe renal or hepatic impairment
monitoring: Sedation and signs of opioid toxicity

title: Cardiovascular Risk Assessment
sourceTitle: Cardiovascular disease: risk assessment and reduction, including lipid modification
edition: NG238, published 14 December 2023; recommendations retrieved 12 October 2026
scope: Adults without established cardiovascular disease being assessed for primary prevention, with selected lipid assessment, statin eligibility and monitoring recommendations.
gaps: QRISK3 is calibrated for a UK population and requires Saudi/local risk-model and formulary review. NICE names atorvastatin 20 mg but the cited recommendations do not provide a complete route, frequency, duration, interaction and contraindication set. Pregnancy is an explicit contraindication; product information and organ-function adjustments remain required.

investigations.test: QRISK3 10-year cardiovascular risk calculation
investigations.question: What is the estimated 10-year CVD risk for an adult aged 25 to 84 without established CVD?
investigations.finding: A QRISK3 result supports shared prevention decisions; 10% or more is NICE's threshold for offering atorvastatin 20 mg in primary prevention.
investigations.rationale: NICE recommends QRISK3 in the specified population while recognising groups in whom risk may be underestimated or a tool should not be used.
investigations.timeframe: At formal risk assessment and after meaningful risk-factor change

investigations.test: Full lipid profile and baseline statin safety assessment
investigations.question: Are dyslipidaemia, secondary causes or baseline factors relevant to treatment present?
investigations.finding: Total cholesterol, HDL, non-HDL, LDL and triglycerides, plus diabetes status, renal function, transaminases and indicated TSH inform treatment and referral.
investigations.rationale: NICE specifies these measures before statin treatment and for specialist referral decisions.
investigations.timeframe: Before starting lipid-lowering treatment

investigations.test: Lipid profile and liver transaminase monitoring
investigations.question: Is treatment producing the intended lipid response without clinically important liver abnormality?
investigations.finding: Repeat results support adherence, response and safety review.
investigations.rationale: NICE recommends full lipid profile and transaminase testing 2 to 3 months after starting or changing treatment, with transaminase testing at 12 months.
investigations.timeframe: 2 to 3 months after starting or changing treatment; transaminases at 12 months

actions.instruction: Discuss lifestyle change, personal preferences, comorbidity, polypharmacy, frailty and life expectancy before deciding on a statin; offer atorvastatin 20 mg when 10-year QRISK3 is 10% or more.
Do not use statins in pregnancy; stop if pregnancy is possible, stop 3 months before attempting conception and do not restart until breastfeeding is finished.

title: Cataract Surgery Assessment and Preparation
edition: NG77, published 26 October 2017; surveillance reviewed 20 May 2025
scope: Adults aged 18 or older being considered and prepared for cataract surgery, including referral discussion, biometry and complication-risk assessment.
gaps: The source does not provide a complete perioperative medicine, eye-drop, anaesthetic dose or contraindication set. Ophthalmology assessment, product information, anticoagulant handling, infection prevention and Saudi/local surgical protocols require reconciliation.

investigations.test: Vision and quality-of-life assessment
investigations.question: How does the cataract affect daily function, and does the person want surgery after discussing benefits and harms?
investigations.finding: The person's functional impact and preferences determine referral; visual acuity alone must not restrict access.
investigations.rationale: NICE bases referral on shared discussion of vision, quality of life, bilateral involvement and patient preference.
investigations.timeframe: At referral assessment

investigations.test: Optical biometry with keratometry
investigations.question: What axial length and corneal curvature should inform intraocular lens calculation?
investigations.finding: Optical biometry and keratometry provide the standard measurements; ultrasound is used when optical measurement is unavailable or inaccurate.
investigations.rationale: NICE recommends these measurements for people having cataract surgery.
investigations.timeframe: During preoperative assessment

investigations.test: Validated surgical complication-risk stratification
investigations.question: Is the person at increased risk during or after surgery?
investigations.finding: A validated risk result informs counselling, supervision and planning.
investigations.rationale: NICE recommends considering a validated algorithm and explaining the result to the patient.
investigations.timeframe: Before surgery

actions.instruction: Give tailored oral and written information on procedure, risks, benefits, alternatives, recovery, postoperative support and warning symptoms.
actions.timeframe: At referral, preoperative review and discharge

actions.instruction: Do not restrict access to cataract surgery solely by visual-acuity threshold.

title: Cervical Cancer Screening and Follow-Up
sourceTitle: NHS Cervical Screening Programme: introduction and programme policy
scope: People with a cervix aged 24.5 to 64 in the English NHS screening programme; limited to primary HPV screening, routine interval and selected follow-up principles.
gaps: This English programme is not a Saudi screening schedule. Eligibility, age range, interval, sample method, laboratory workflow, referral thresholds and post-treatment follow-up must be reconciled with current Saudi policy. Symptoms require diagnostic assessment rather than routine screening.

investigations.test: Primary high-risk HPV cervical screening with cytology triage
investigations.question: Is high-risk HPV present and, if so, does reflex cytology identify a referral pathway?
investigations.finding: A negative primary hrHPV result supports routine recall; a positive result triggers cytology triage and programme-defined surveillance or colposcopy.
investigations.rationale: The NHS programme uses primary hrHPV screening because of higher sensitivity, with cytology triage to preserve specificity.
investigations.timeframe: At the programme-defined screening interval

investigations.test: Eligibility and prior-result review
investigations.question: Does age, cervical status, previous hrHPV positivity or prior abnormality change routine recall?
investigations.finding: The English programme first invites at 24.5 years and uses a 5-year interval after a negative primary hrHPV result, with exceptions for recent positivity and non-routine follow-up.
investigations.rationale: Programme policy defines different recall based on age and previous results.
investigations.timeframe: Before invitation, sampling and discharge from follow-up

actions.instruction: Use the current local programme pathway for sample processing, result communication, surveillance and colposcopy referral; do not apply an English interval without Saudi reconciliation.
Assess cervical-cancer symptoms through a diagnostic pathway rather than waiting for or relying on a screening test.

title: Childhood Immunisation and Catch-Up
sourceTitle: Saudi Ministry of Health: Children Vaccinations
edition: Saudi MOH public guidance, retrieved 12 October 2026
locator: Before vaccination; postponing vaccination; when to consult a doctor; timing and catch-up advice
scope: Children attending routine immunisation or catch-up review in Saudi Arabia; limited to record review, timing, deferral and safety screening rather than a product-by-product schedule.
gaps: The retrieved page does not provide the full current national antigen-by-age table, product-specific dose volume, route, minimum intervals or complete contraindications. The current Saudi national schedule, product information and specialist guidance for immunocompromised children must be checked before administration.

investigations.test: Immunisation-record and age review
investigations.question: Which scheduled doses are documented, due or delayed?
investigations.finding: The record and the current national schedule identify due and catch-up needs without restarting prior valid doses.
investigations.rationale: Saudi MOH advises bringing the child's record and maintaining age-scheduled vaccination.
investigations.timeframe: At every vaccination visit

investigations.test: Pre-vaccination allergy, acute-illness, immunosuppression and neurological-history screen
investigations.question: Is there a condition requiring deferral, specialist advice or product-specific contraindication review?
investigations.finding: Severe prior reaction, severe component allergy, immunodeficiency, immunosuppressive treatment or relevant neurological history may change the plan; mild illness or mild fever alone may not prevent vaccination.
investigations.rationale: Saudi MOH lists these checks and directs clinician consultation where safety questions exist.
investigations.timeframe: Immediately before each vaccine

actions.instruction: Follow the current Saudi national immunisation schedule and arrange catch-up from the last documented valid dose rather than automatically restarting a series.

Obtain clinician or specialist advice before vaccination after a severe previous reaction, with severe component allergy, immunodeficiency, immunosuppressive treatment or relevant neurological disorder.
